I am the customer that opened two support cases with RedHat about the nios_txt_record module:

CASE 02473253: Ansible module nios_txt_record won't add TXT records if multiple TXT records already exist.
CASE 02473244: Ansible nios_txt_record module replaces existing TXT records instead of adding additional records.

Both issues are likely caused by the same problem.  In the documentation for [nios_txt_record](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/modules/nios_txt_record_module.html#nios-txt-record-module), the view and name parameters are required, but the text parameter is not.  This is wrong. 

The TXT record type is just like the A record type, there can be many records with the same name but different values.  For this reason, in the nios_a_record module, the ipaddress parameter is a required field.  The text parameter in nios_txt_record should also be a required field and the nios_txt_record module should be looking at the combination of the view:name:text parameters values to determine if an operation is idempotent.

If I run the following playbook:

`---

- hosts: example_grid_primary
  connection: local

  tasks:
    - name: Add/Delete TXT Records
      nios_txt_record:
        provider: "{{nios_provider}}"
        comment: CHG0000000
        view: External
        name: _example.example.com
        text: thequickbrownfoxjumpedoverthelazydog
        state: present

    - name: Add/Delete TXT Records
      nios_txt_record:
        provider: "{{nios_provider}}"
        comment: CHG0000000
        view: External
        name: _example.example.com
        text: fourscoreandsevenyearsagoourfathers
        state: present

...
`
I should get this as my response to a TXT query for _example.example.com:

_example.example.com.	900	IN	TXT	"thequickbrownfoxjumpedoverthelazydog"
_example.example.com.	900	IN	TXT	"fourscoreandsevenyearsagoourfathers"

Instead I get:

_example.example.com.	900	IN	TXT	"fourscoreandsevenyearsagoourfathers"

The above example only works if there isn't already a TXT record with the name "_example.example.com."

If there are already multiple TXT records with the same name because they were imported or added via the Infoblox admin interface, then when you try to add another TXT record with the same name using the nios_txt_record module, you get an error:

[add_txt_records_errors.txt](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/files/3628087/add_txt_records_errors.txt)

An example if where you need multiple TXT records with the same name is when you use Amazon's Simple Email Service.  [Amazon SES uses TXT records to verify email domains.](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-txt-records.html)  AWS requires a different TXT record with the same name but different value for each AWS region you operate in.

When deciding priority for bug fixes, keep in mind  if a customer today operating in only one AWS region uses the nios_txt_module to add a second TXT record for AWS SES so they can operate in a second region, their first SES TXT record will be replaced with the second and they will experience an email failure with all their email in their original AWS region.

We only avoided this fate because we already operate in multiple AWS regions and had multiple TXT records with the same name, so this bug's second failure mode actually saved us from having a Severity 1 outage.

Does the update TXT module work if there are already multiple TXT records with the same name?  The old module would crash if there was more than one existing TXT record with the same name.  Your first test started with 0 records, the second with 1 record.  You should do a third to see if it works with more than one TXT record with the same name.

Also, can you remove a given TXT record without impacting the remaining records?

> Does the update TXT module work if there are already multiple TXT records with the same name? The old module would crash if there was more than one existing TXT record with the same name. Your first test started with 0 records, the second with 1 record. You should do a third to see if it works with more than one TXT record with the same name.
>
> Also, can you remove a given TXT record without impacting the remaining records?

Maybe I simplified the use-case a bit too much. I did test those scenarios while preparing PRs for Ansible 2.8 and 2.9, and all of the things you are asking about here are solved in the `devel` and `stable-2.9` branches.

The module crashed previously because it always excepted that the backend has at most one matching entry. Now that the `text` field is part of the parameters that are used to look up the existing entries, the at-most-one invariant always holds, and the crash cannot happen anymore. This same line of reasoning also explains why it is now possible to remove only one specific TXT record without touching anything else.

And while I am replying, Ansible 2.8 may not get fixed because it is currently accepting only critical bug fixes. So it is up to the release manager to decide if this issue is critical enough to warrant a fix in 2.8.
